@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1A8MDQ9NTZX4A0N8JZBA4XN
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8180'
+title: 'Real-model test: a cold MetadataSearcher returns only catalog ids'
+---
+## What
+
+The first of the two real-model tests. It is the highest-value one on the board: it is the only thing that would catch the class of defect FoundationModelsRanker hit in `d333d07`.
+
+File to create:
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMetadataRegistryIntegrationTests/ColdSelectionRealModelTests.swift`
+
+Build a `MetadataSearcher` in `.selection` mode over the fixture catalog from `^jzba4xn`, with:
+
+```swift
+SelectionConfig(
+    model: { instructions in
+        LanguageModelSession(model: .default, instructions: instructions)
+    },
+    preamble: .librarianDefault
+)
+```
+
+Then run `search(intent:limit:)` and assert every returned id is in the catalog, and that no `.unknownSelectedId` diagnostic fired — collect diagnostics through the `onDiagnostic:` parameter.
+
+### Two design constraints that are the whole point of this test
+
+**1. A FRESH `MetadataSearcher` per query.** Not one searcher reused across a parameterized run. FoundationModelsRanker measured this exact defect: on a cold session the on-device model returned `{"ids":[]}` for some queries, 0 of 5 runs succeeding, while the same query on a warm session succeeded every time. A suite that reuses one searcher **cannot see it**, because `LanguageModelSession.fork()` returns `self`, so the session is warm from call two onward. Construct the searcher inside the test body, per query.
+
+**2. At least one query phrased as an imperative.** The failing queries in Ranker's data were exactly the ones phrased as an order — "record my staged changes as a new commit" scored 0/5 before the fix. Interrogative phrasings ("how do I list or delete a branch") were less affected. Use a parameterized test with a mix, and make sure an imperative is among them.
+
+Treat Ranker's causal story as unproven — they were explicit that restating the framing in plain prose worked worse than the Markdown heading, so *why* it helps is not established, over four fixture queries and one model version. The structural point stands regardless: cold, imperative, one query at a time is the shape that fails.
+
+### Scope
+
+Under-budget cached-root path only. Do not add an over-budget case; that path's mechanics are already at 97% line coverage through fakes, and the model-behavior half belongs to FoundationModelsRanker.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] The test constructs a new `MetadataSearcher` for every query, inside the test body.
+- [ ] At least one query is phrased as an imperative.
+- [ ] Every returned id is asserted to be a member of the fixture catalog's id set.
+- [ ] No `.unknownSelectedId` diagnostic is recorded for any query.
+- [ ] At least one match is returned for each on-topic query — an empty result is a failure, because empty is the exact symptom of the defect this test guards.
+- [ ] The test calls `ModelAvailability.requireAvailable()` first.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/Tests/.../ColdSelectionRealModelTests.swift` — a parameterized `@Test(arguments:)` over three or more intents, at least one imperative.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests`. All queries return at least one valid catalog id.
+- [ ] Run it three times. Record the pass rate per query in a comment on this card. A query that is not stable across three runs must be replaced or its flakiness recorded, never silently retried.
+- [ ] Prove the assertion can fail: temporarily assert against a catalog id set that excludes a real answer, confirm the failure, revert.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

+    - commit: e687da5 test(integration): add cold MetadataSearcher real-model selection test

+
+    ### The three things the reviewer verified, not assumed
+    1. **The searcher really is per query.** `catalog`, `recorded` and `searcher` are all locals of the test body. The only suite-level state is an immutable `[String]` of intents — no session. Each case's `LanguageModelSession` is built inside a `SelectionConfig` constructed fresh for that case. Nothing warm crosses cases, which is the whole point: `fork()` returns `self`, so a hoisted searcher would be warm from call two and blind to the defect this test guards.
+    2. **The non-empty assertion is reachable and ordered first**, so an empty return fails on that line alone.
+    3. **The diagnostic filter survives company.** `compactMap` with `guard case .unknownSelectedId` drops every other case, so an `.unknownSelectedId` sitting among 55 `.embeddingUnavailable` entries is still extracted and still fails.
+
+    ### One honest limit on the RED, recorded by the reviewer
+    `limit: catalog.count` binds the limit to the same catalog, so the empty-catalog RED also drives `limit: 0`. That proves the assertion is **reachable**, not specifically that a populated catalog with an empty model answer would fail it. The real-path evidence for that is `^nwt7nz4`'s off-topic control returning empty 5/5 over a populated catalog. Not a finding — the binding is deliberate and documented in the file — but worth knowing the proof is two-part.
+
+    ### Design note carried forward
+    The diagnostic sink is `OSAllocatedUnfairLock<[MetadataDiagnostic]>`, not the root suite's `DiagnosticRecorder` (unreachable — a test target is not a product) and not `Synchronization.Mutex`, which is `~Copyable` and so cannot be captured by the `@escaping @Sendable` `onDiagnostic` closure.
